text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD-DB-8001 fired for service=redis-main cluster=cache-east-1 — reason: maxclients reached (client_connections=10240, maxclients=10240). Auto-retries failing, latency spike observed. Paging oncall schedule: eng-oncall primary.

alex.chen: acked via PD. I'm looking. seeing a lot of `client>idle` connections in `redis-cli info clients`.

maria.lopez: noticed increased 5xxs from API-frontend tied to cache timeouts. Customer impact: some write-heavy features failing, ~2% user errors. dashboard: https://console.redwood/metrics/cache-east-1

raghav: thanks. is this after the deployment @alex?

alex.chen: no deploys in last 30m per deploy-bot. likely traffic ramp. digging into pgbouncer/proxy layer for connection fanout.

sre-runbook-bot: runbook: Cache connection saturation -> https://runbooks.internal/cache-conn-saturation. Recommended first steps: 1) Identify high-traffic clients 2) Enable conn-limiter on proxy 3) Fail open to readonly for non-critical endpoints.

alex.chen: running `kubectl exec -it redis-main-0 -- redis-cli CLIENT LIST | grep -E "^id=" | wc -l` to confirm. output ~10240, matches maxclients.

maria.lopez: can we temporarily bump maxclients on this shard?

alex.chen: we can, but it's risky across nodes (mem increase + file descriptors). prefer reducing inbound concurrency at proxy. trying `kubectl -n infra scale deployment cache-proxy-east --replicas=4` to add capacity.

alex.chen: scaled cache-proxy-east to 4. also applying quick rate-limit rule on apiproxy: `rate-limit: 150r/s per-service` for write-heavy endpoints.

oncall-next: pinging next oncall to prep: @emily.prod FYI, potential customer impact, may need product comms if sustained.

emily.prod: on it, thanks. collecting which tenants hit errors, will DM list shortly.

raghav: any signs of idle connections not closing? Could be client library bug opening connections and not reusing.

alex.chen: running a quick query on pgbouncer-like proxy logs: `grep "CONNECT" /var/log/proxy/cache-proxy-east.log | awk '{print $5}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head` to find top clients. found three internal workers with huge connection churn: transformer-worker-prod (6000 conns), ingestion-svc (1500), batch-hydra (900).

maria.lopez: transformer-worker-prod deployed a new batch job earlier today, possibly unbounded connections. can we throttle that job?

alex.chen: issuing kill on excessive job pods: `kubectl delete pod transformer-worker-prod-zzzz --namespace=jobs` (scaled down the cron to 2 concurrent jobs).

incident-bot: PD note: alert escalated to level-2 after 8m without mitigation.

alex.chen: after scaling proxies and killing batch pods, client count dropped to ~5300 within 3m. latency improving.

maria.lopez: API 5xxs dropping from 2% -> 0.3%. customer-impact window estimate: 00:04:32 -> 00:20:15 UTC (approx).

raghav: we should still follow up: 1) ensure transformer_worker uses connection pool/keepalive, 2) add circuit breaker in proxy for excess connections, 3) investigate why client's retry logic opens new conns instead of reusing.

sre-runbook-bot: checklist updated in runbook entry with performed actions and links to logs: https://runbooks.internal/cache-conn-saturation/1766004321-event

alex.chen: creating a short-lived pprof/trace for transformer-worker to confirm connection code path. also opened PR to add pooling. PR: https://git.internal/ingestion/PR-4521

emily.prod: product note: no high-dollar customers affected based on initial tenant list, mostly internal batch jobs and free-tier customers. will draft a short status update if this holds.

maria.lopez: should we increase `maxclients` by 2k temporarily to buy breathing room?

raghav: if we bump, coordinate with infra for ulimit/fd and monitor swap. prefer not to until we confirm connection leak addressed.

alex.chen: agree. holding on bump. I'll leave scaled proxy count up for 30m then consider scaling down.

oncall-next: prepping handoff notes for next shift. Alex, can you add a short summary + next steps to the oncall doc?

alex.chen: done: "Scaled cache proxies -> reduced connection fanout; terminated runaway transformer job; enabled write-rate limit on apiproxy; monitoring. Next: PR to fix pooling, consider conn-limiter in proxy, no config changes to maxclients yet." link: https://wiki.redwood/oncall/handovers/1766004321

incident-bot: PD incident PD-DB-8001 acknowledged by alex.chen at 1766004340.

maria.lopez: closing customer-impact window to 00:20:15 UTC; continuing monitoring for 30m.

raghav: recommended postmortem: short postmortem + action to add connection pooling library checks in CI for transformer-worker. tagging infra and ingestion teams.

alex.chen: marking this thread resolved for now. will update if we see a regression. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: PD incident PD-DB-8001 resolved at 1766007623 by alex.chen (auto-close after ack + mitigation).

emily.prod: thanks all, I'll send out a brief status note to affected customers and attach the handoff link.

alex.chen: thumbs.

maria.lopez: great job everyone. :tada:
